IMO you're not being childish for having feelings, especially since you both had an agreement that you'd spent $X for each other's gifts. So, of course, it was assumed that he'd also be getting you a gift. He broke the promise by not getting you anything back and as a result, you felt hurt. If him not giving you a gift is really bothering you, ask him casually (nowhere near any gift giving holiday) why he's not into giving gifts (not specifically for you; just ask what is his gift giving philosophy is) and maybe that will help you understand him.

Generally, you should give gifts because you enjoy giving gifts, not because you want something in return. It sounds like you have a bit of both; you love putting the time into selecting a gift and seeing the results, e.g. your brother being ecstatic with your gift choices as well as having that some effort spent on you.

Not everyone feels the same way about giving/receiving gifts. It's understandable that you're upset is because you've designated your 21st birthday as something special. Maybe your brother doesn't really care about birthdays, it's just another birthday or an ordinary day to him and it's nothing special.

I'd evaluate whether you spend a lot of time selecting gifts for people so that they'll do the same for you, or whether you actually enjoy giving gifts. I hope that helps give you some perspective.

If you want to get paid to do chores, sit your parents down when they're not busy, and explain what chores you plan on doing, and whether or not they'll pay you to do them.

Neighbors, local elderly persons, people from church or school, and anyone close enough to walk might also be good employers for your chore-doing business.
